report.summary: Chunk 1 of 2 for report.py: defines constants, helper functions, and two main render functions (render_tier1 and render_arms) for producing ASCII eval tables with provenance breakdowns and disclaimers. All claims about ASCII-only rendering and exclusion of errored/focus-withheld tasks are verified as kept; claims about module policy or external module behavior are uncheckable. The render_arms function appears truncated at chunk boundary.
risks: render_arms (line 250-253) | medium | render_arms function appears truncated; the errored section is started but not finished in this chunk. | Verify that the full function in the next chunk completes the errored block.

handoff.purpose: Render eval results as ASCII tables with provenance breakdown and disclaimer notes.

symbols.name: _PROVENANCE_NOTE
symbols.note: Dict mapping provenance keys to disclaimer strings.

symbols.name: _rule
symbols.note: Builds a separator line for ASCII table.

symbols.name: _row
symbols.note: Builds a data row for ASCII table.

symbols.name: _pct
symbols.note: Formats a fraction as percentage string.

claims.text: No unicode box-drawing, no fancy glyphs: only ``+ - |`` so it prints on a raw Windows console.
claims.why: All table functions use only '+', '-', '|' and spaces; no Unicode box-drawing characters are present.

claims.text: Framing is honest: this is a small private directional eval, recall is necessary-not-sufficient, Tier 2 needs a runtime, and -- the point of this module -- "hand_reachable" recall is partly self-graded and MUST NOT be blended with independently-derived recall into one headline number.
claims.why: The docstring makes claims about the module's purpose and policy, but the code only renders data; it does not enforce blending or non-blending. The blending policy is not implemented here.

claims.text: Plain-English disclaimer per provenance -- printed on every render that includes a "hand_reachable" bucket. This is the single most important line in this file: it is what stops the eval from overclaiming.
claims.why: _PROVENANCE_NOTE is defined and used in _provenance_breakdown_lines, which is called by both render_tier1 and render_arms. The disclaimer is printed for each provenance.

claims.text: PARTIALLY SELF-GRADED: a human picked these labels AND verified them reachable by running the same slicer being graded. Treat this recall as an upper bound / sanity check, NOT independent proof the slicer works.
claims.why: The string exactly matches the code.

claims.text: INDEPENDENT: labels derived from what an on-disk diff literally changed -- no graph walk involved. This recall is not self-graded.
claims.why: The string exactly matches the code.

claims.text: INDEPENDENT: labels derived from git co-change (files that change together) -- no graph walk involved. This recall is not self-graded.
claims.why: The string exactly matches the code.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD (lane A1) -- honest, ASCII-only accounting for tasks where the unconditional secret floor fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file (see harness._is_focus_withheld / slice.py's FOCUS GATE). Neither a pass (no slice text was ever compared to must_include) nor a recall miss (the label was never even attempted) -- its own bucket, excluded from every mean/count above. Absent (result.get) for any hand-built result dict that predates this field, and adds no lines when there are none.
claims.why: The function uses result.get('focus_withheld_ids') and returns empty list if not present or empty. It generates lines only when ids exist.

claims.text: Shared renderer for the "PROVENANCE BREAKDOWN" block used by both Tier 1 and the arms report. Always shows both tiers (even when empty) and always prints the honesty note -- this block is the deliverable of this sprint.
claims.why: The function prints the header, iterates over all provenances and both tiers, includes the note for each provenance, and appends the quarantine note. It is called by both render_tier1 and render_arms.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall/compression/slice_tokens/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they get their own ERRORED section below, not a row in this recall/compression table. FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (see harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section below.
claims.why: The loop skips tasks with 'error' in t or t.get('focus_withheld'). Errored tasks are later reported in a separate section via result.get('errored').

claims.text: Healthy (non-errored, non-focus-withheld) misses only -- an errored task has no "missed" list at all (it never got as far as measuring recall); a focus-withheld task has none either (the fence refused before recall was ever measured). Both are reported in their own unmissable sections, not folded in here as a miss.
claims.why: The misses list filters out tasks with 'error' or 'focus_withheld'. The code matches the description.

claims.text: Absent entirely (result.get, not result[...]) for any pre-existing caller that hand-built a Tier-1 result dict without this key -- and always absent when there are zero errored tasks, so this block adds NO lines to that report.
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored') and only adds lines if the list is non-empty.

claims.text: A/B/C: distilled slice vs whole-repo concat vs BM25 retrieval. Model-free (recall via substring match, no LLM), so this runs offline every time.
claims.why: The claim about model-free recall via substring match is not verifiable from this chunk; it describes behavior in other modules.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall_A/tokens_A/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they are reported in their own section below, not in this table. FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section.
claims.why: The healthy list filters out tasks with 'error' or 'focus_withheld'. Errored tasks are reported later via result.get('errored').

claims.text: c_beats_a is tie-inclusive (recall_C >= recall_A, see harness.eval_task_arms) so this block -- not the "no" cells under the C>=A column -- is where a tie surfaces. A tie ("BM25 matches the product's recall at equal cost") is the commercially damning case, not merely a strict loss for A.
claims.why: The claim about tie-inclusive definition refers to harness.eval_task_arms, which is not in this chunk. The code uses t['c_beats_a'] but cannot verify its semantics.

claims.text: ERRORED section -- same rationale as render_tier1's: excluded from every arm/aggregate above, never silently dropped. Absent when there are none.
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored') and only adds lines if non-empty.

observations.what: render_arms uses result.get('errored') but the chunk ends before the block is closed; the function may be incomplete.
